author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can see which veterinarians hold each specialty
summary: A read-only page at /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it, named first name then last name. All specialties render on one page.
acceptance_criteria: opening /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows, by its stored name
each specialty lists the veterinarians holding it, named first name then last name (for example "Helen Leary")
a veterinarian holding no specialty appears nowhere on the page
a specialty held by no veterinarian still appears, with no veterinarian named under it
a clinic that knows no specialties still renders the page, listing none
all specialties appear together on one page, without paging
specialties, and the veterinarians within each, appear in a stable order rather than an arbitrary one
non_goals: managing veterinarians or their specialties through the application (NG-2, unchanged)
a navigation entry or any link to the page from elsewhere: it is reachable by its address alone
notes: NG-2 is unchanged and no Non-Goals row was touched, so no scope_overrides apply. REQ-LANG-002 applies to the new page: its wording is bundled and present in every supported language. REQ-SYS-001 is unaffected — the new page carries the existing navigation, and nothing links to it. Three open questions are recorded in docs/prd.md#open-questions (ordering, empty states, a future entry point); each was taken at its narrowest reading rather than escalated, per the dispatch.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice lands entirely inside the existing vet feature package and uses only patterns already in force. It needs one adjustment to durable memory's picture: system-design.md records Specialty as reachable only through Vet, and the acceptance criterion 'a specialty held by no veterinarian still appears' cannot be met from the vet side. Add a narrow SpecialtyRepository so specialties are readable independently. Everything else is precedented. Basis for this claim is a direct read of the vet package (no IDE oracle connected): VetRepository.java declares only findAll() and findAll(Pageable); Specialty.java is a bare NamedEntity with no inverse association; the vet-to-specialty ManyToMany is declared only on Vet.java:47.
integration_points: New GET route /specialties.html served by a new package-private SpecialtyController in org.springframework.samples.petclinic.vet. VetController is not modified, so the /vets.html and /vets routes and their tests are untouched.

New SpecialtyRepository extending org.springframework.data.repository.Repository<Specialty, Integer> with one read method, mirroring VetRepository's narrow shape rather than PetTypeRepository's JpaRepository. The narrow base class carries no save or delete, so NG-2 is enforced by the type rather than by convention.

The read of veterinarians reuses the existing VetRepository.findAll(). Same method, same @Cacheable("vets") key, so the new page shares the cache CacheConfiguration already declares and adds no cache and no second query path.

New Thymeleaf template under templates/vets/, rendered through fragments/layout.html. Pass 'specialties' as the layout's menu argument: it matches no menuItem, so no navigation entry is highlighted, which is the correct rendering for a page nothing links to.
No PetClinicRuntimeHints change is expected; Spring Boot's Thymeleaf auto-configuration supplies the template resource hints, and messages/* is already registered.

patterns.description: Narrow read-only repository over org.springframework.data.repository.Repository. SpecialtyRepository copies this shape exactly, minus the @Cacheable annotation.
getSpecialties() sorts by name in Java, not in SQL. This is the governing precedent for the ordering decision below, and it sits in the same package as the new code.
Controller reads a repository, puts a list on the model, returns a view name. SpecialtyController follows this, without the pagination helpers.
th:each over a model list inside the shared layout fragment. The new template is the same shape with an outer loop over specialties.
@WebMvcTest slice with @MockitoBean repositories and MockMvc. SpecialtyControllerTests copies it with both SpecialtyRepository and VetRepository mocked.

risks.risk: N+1 and lazy-loading trap. spring.jpa.open-in-view is false (application.properties:11), so any association first touched during rendering throws.
risks.mitigation: Vet.specialties is FetchType.EAGER, so it is populated inside the repository's read-only transaction and the cached Vet instances arrive at the template fully loaded. Reuse VetRepository.findAll() rather than adding a query: the per-vet specialty selects the EAGER mapping may issue are already paid by REQ-VET-001 and absorbed by the vets cache, so this page adds none. Do not add an inverse vets collection to Specialty: it would make a shared mapping bidirectional and risk an eager cycle, for a read-only page. Do not write a JPQL join from Vet to its specialties as the source of the specialty list: it drops specialties held by no veterinarian and fails an acceptance criterion.

risks.risk: Grouping by Specialty instance would silently misgroup. BaseEntity declares no equals or hashCode, so entities compare by identity. Specialty instances reached through the cached Vet graph are different objects from those returned by SpecialtyRepository.
risks.mitigation: Key the grouping on the specialty identifier, never on the Specialty instance and never on the name (the specialties table has an index on name but no unique constraint, so duplicate stored names are representable).

risks.risk: Vendor-divergent ordering. The schemas already diverge on collation, and case-sensitivity divergence between H2 and PostgreSQL is a recorded Known Defect. A SQL ORDER BY would repeat that class of bug on an ordering the acceptance criteria assert.
risks.mitigation: Order in the projection with an explicit Java comparator, so the H2-backed test suite observes the same order every vendor produces.

risks.risk: The page is unbounded: every specialty and every veterinarian on one response, by requirement.
risks.mitigation: Accepted. NG-2 leaves no in-application growth path, and the seeded scale is three specialties and six veterinarians. Revisit only if a write path for veterinarians is ever introduced.

risks.risk: The two repository reads run in separate read-only transactions, so they are not a consistent snapshot.
risks.mitigation: Accepted. There is no in-application write path for either table, and rows are seeded at startup.

risks.risk: A new plain projection type exposed to Thymeleaf may need a reflection hint under GraalVM native image. The test suite is @DisabledInNativeImage, so it cannot catch this.
risks.mitigation: If a native-image build fails on property access, register the projection type in PetClinicRuntimeHints. Low severity: the default build does not exercise native image.

notes: ORDERING, decided here as a design call rather than left to the implementer. The PRD leaves it open and the criterion demands only a stable order, but an unpinned order makes the assertion flaky, so it is fixed: specialties by name case-insensitively (String.CASE_INSENSITIVE_ORDER, locale-independent), then by identifier as tiebreaker; veterinarians within a specialty by last name, then first name, both case-insensitively, then by identifier. Both comparators live in the projection, in Java. Rationale: the veterinarian ordering cannot come from SQL anyway, since the grouping is assembled in memory from the cached VetRepository.findAll(), and splitting one ordering rule across SQL and Java would put it in two places. Vet.getSpecialties() is the in-package precedent for sorting in Java; PetTypeRepository's ORDER BY query is the counterexample, and it does not govern because it feeds a dropdown where vendor divergence is invisible. || WHERE THE PROJECTION BELONGS. Not in the controller. architecture-principles.md's Web controller row admits no business rule, and its validation checklist states the existing controller deviation does not extend to new rules. Introduce SpecialtyDirectory, a package-private immutable value object in the vet package, built by a static factory from (Collection<Specialty>, Collection<Vet>) and exposing an ordered list of entries, each carrying a specialty name and the ordered full names of the veterinarians holding it. The persistence-entity exception does not cover it (the framework does not instantiate it), so it realizes the closed Domain Core properties in full: a record with List.copyOf in the compact constructor. Carrying display-ready strings rather than entity references keeps it equal by value and makes the full-name rule ('Helen Leary', first then last) a tested rule rather than template concatenation. Value object and Repository are both In force in the pattern catalog, so no ADR is needed; the exact record shape is a bounded implementer choice. || I18N. I18nPropertiesSyncTest.checkNonInternationalizedStrings scans every .html under src/main and fails on any >literal< without #{ or th:text, so every visible string in the new template must be a message key. Reuse existing keys before adding any: 'specialties' for the heading, 'name', 'vets', and 'none' for the empty case. Each new key must be added to messages.properties and the nine non-English locale bundles; messages_en.properties is exempt by the test's fallback logic. checkI18nPropertyFilesAreInSync fails the build on a partial translation, which is how REQ-LANG-002 is enforced. || TEST SHAPE. Put the semantics in SpecialtyDirectoryTests, a plain JUnit test with real Vet and Specialty objects and no Spring context: listing every specialty, omitting a veterinarian holding none, keeping a specialty held by none, the empty clinic, and the ordering. Put the wiring in SpecialtyControllerTests, a @WebMvcTest(SpecialtyController.class) slice with both repositories as @MockitoBean and MockMvc asserting status, view name, model attribute, and rendered content for the full-name and one-page criteria. This keeps the pyramid weighted to unit tests and confines the sanctioned mock to MockMvc plus the two repository seams the existing VetControllerTests already mocks. || DOCS. No edit to docs/system-design.md or docs/adr/ accompanies this verdict. The Contracts table is a current-state table and the new types do not exist yet; SpecialtyRepository, SpecialtyController, and SpecialtyDirectory belong in it after the code lands, through doc-sync, along with REQ-VET-003 on the Vet, Specialty, and VetRepository rows. || AUTOFIX AUDIT. No design-doc-autofix records in the log; nothing to audit.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: New endpoint takes no request-derived input: GET /specialties.html in SpecialtyController has no path variable, query parameter, or form binding, so the injection, mass-assignment, and path-traversal rows of security-principles.md cannot be reached from it. No @InitBinder is needed because nothing is request-bound.

No SQL is authored: SpecialtyRepository.findAll() is a Spring Data derived query on the narrow Repository base, matching the VetRepository pattern. No string-concatenated query text anywhere in the diff.

NG-2 (read-only) holds by type, not by convention: SpecialtyRepository extends Repository<Specialty, Integer> rather than CrudRepository/JpaRepository, so no save/delete/write method exists on the interface at all. Swept the diff and the vet package for any other write path introduced by this change; none.

Output escaping is intact throughout src/main/resources/templates/vets/specialtyList.html: every user-derived value (entry.specialtyName, vetName) renders through th:text, which applies Thymeleaf HTML escaping. Swept the new template and the whole templates/vets/ directory for th:utext, th:inline, and inline javascript blocks: zero occurrences. Stored specialty or veterinarian names containing markup render as inert text, so no stored-XSS path is opened.

No SpEL injection surface: every Thymeleaf expression in the new template is a static, literally-authored expression over model attributes. No user-derived string is evaluated as an expression, and no template name is composed from input (the view name 'vets/specialtyList' is a constant).

No data-exposure delta against the baseline in system-design.md#security-context: veterinarian full names and their specialties are already published unauthenticated at /vets.html and /vets by VetController. The new page is a reverse projection of exactly that data set, adds no new field, and reaches no other entity (owners, pets, visits are untouched). The application-wide absence of authentication is the recorded demonstration baseline, not a finding against this change.

No secrets introduced: swept the full change set for credential-shaped material (token, password, secret, key, connection strings, datasource properties). The diff touches no configuration or profile file; build.gradle and the application-*.properties are unchanged.

Supply chain unchanged: scripts/changeset.sh --name-only lists no build file, no dependency declaration, and no repository declaration, so the change adds no artifact and cannot alter resolution. The four dependency checks in system-design.md are not triggered by this diff.

No unsafe deserialization or resource resolution: SpecialtyDirectory is built in-process from repository reads, holds only String and List<String>, and no endpoint accepts serialized object input. Nothing in the change composes a filesystem or classpath path.
Error handling leaks nothing new: the handler declares no catch block and constructs no exception message, so it cannot carry a connection string or internal detail into the error page.

Unpaginated rendering is a product decision recorded in the PRD (all specialties on one page, no paging) over a small, staff-curated table that no unauthenticated caller can grow; it is a resource-consideration rather than a security finding, and leaves the application no weaker than the /vets.html baseline it mirrors.

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: Veterinarian full names for a specialty are joined by concatenating each with a trailing space (`th:text="${vetName + ' '}"` on a `th:each` span) rather than with an explicit, visible separator. For a specialty held by more than one veterinarian this renders as an unbroken run of names, e.g. 'Helen Leary Rafael Ortega', with nothing to tell a reader where one full name ends and the next begins — exactly the ambiguity the full-name rule (first name then last name) exists to avoid. No test exercises the multi-holder case, so the ambiguity is currently invisible to the suite.
findings.fix: Join the names with a visible separator, e.g. `th:text="${#strings.listJoin(entry.veterinarianNames, ', ')}"` on a single span instead of one span per name.

approved_aspects: SpecialtyController is package-private with a narrow constructor-injected dependency list and no business rule in the controller body, matching the design block and the Web controller row in architecture-principles.md
SpecialtyRepository mirrors VetRepository's narrow Repository<Specialty, Integer> shape exactly, enforcing read-only access by type

SpecialtyDirectory is a package-private, immutable record (List.copyOf in both compact constructors) that owns the identifier-keyed grouping, the full-name rule, and both ordering comparators, keeping business rules out of the controller and template
Grouping keys on Specialty::getId rather than instance or name, avoiding the identity/duplicate-name traps the design block called out
No inverse Specialty.vets collection and no JPQL join through Vet.specialties; the directory is built from the two existing findAll() reads, reusing the vets cache
Ordering is applied in Java with explicit Comparators (case-insensitive name, then id; case-insensitive last/first name, then id) rather than SQL ORDER BY, avoiding vendor collation divergence
Javadoc on SpecialtyDirectory clearly states the three rules it owns and why; naming follows architecture-principles.md (Repository suffix, Controller suffix, no prohibited suffixes)
New template reuses existing i18n keys (specialties, name, vets, none) rather than adding new ones; checkFormat passes clean

author: change-grader

blast_radius.note: Purely additive: eight new files plus one docs/prd.md edit, 11 hunks across two modules, no sensitive paths, and not one existing production file modified, so no existing route, template, or query path can regress; the only shared surface reused is VetRepository.findAll(), called unchanged with its existing vets cache key.

semantic_surprise.note: Read every hunk of SpecialtyDirectory, SpecialtyController, SpecialtyRepository, and specialtyList.html and found nothing the description would not predict: grouping is by specialty identifier rather than instance or name (entities compare by identity, stored names are not unique), ordering is applied in Java as Vet.getSpecialties() already does, Vet's ManyToMany is FetchType.EAGER so the projection built in the controller is safe under the disabled open-in-view, and both template branches render through escaping th:text; the one latent trap, thenComparing on a null Specialty identifier, is unreachable because both reads return persisted entities.
